title: Skills
text:
Each skill is a single SKILL.md file. Install by copying the folder into ~/.claude/skills/ and restarting Claude Code:
12 of the 18 skills need configuration before first use; the “Needs config?” column below names it for each one. Skill names link to the source on GitHub, where SKILL.md renders cleanly.

title: Skills
text:
Skills overview



Skill
Purpose
Needs config?




archive-raw-data
End-of-collection workflow: export Mongo → JSONL, commit to repo, archive to Zenodo with DOI, optionally drop Mongo data
ZENODO_TOKEN, MONGODB_URI in .env; mongoexport installed


aspredicted
Draft an AsPredicted pre-registration by walking through each field with you
No


data-analysis
Default workflow for cleaning, exploration, visualization
No


gws
Interact with Google Workspace (Drive, Docs, Sheets, Gmail, Calendar) via the gws CLI
Requires gws CLI installed + authed


latex-gdoc-roundtrip
Push a LaTeX paper to a formatted Google Doc for coauthor review; pull edits back
Requires gws CLI


latex-workflow
Build, commit, push a LaTeX paper; coauthors edit in Overleaf
No


log-off
End-of-session ritual — updates todo/comms/current_state and creates a handoff
{WORKSPACE}, {PHONE}


notify-me
Send yourself an iMessage when a long task finishes
{PHONE}; macOS only


opportunity-hunter
Find and rank jobs, grants, prizes, fellowships from your profile
{REPORTS_DIR}; profile in CLAUDE.md


pipeline-audit
Audit a data→code→output→manuscript pipeline for inconsistencies and magic numbers
No


plate-check
Weekly review pulling from Gmail, Calendar, tasks, todo.md; generates a dashboard
{WORKSPACE}, {PHONE}


qualtrics-survey
Build Qualtrics surveys via the API
.env with QUALTRICS_API_TOKEN


quarto-version-toggle
Render one Quarto HTML doc with multiple pre-rendered versions, switchable via buttons
No


render-survey
Scaffold and deploy a full-stack behavioral research web app to Render
Render + Mongo Atlas + OPENAI_API_KEY


research-writing
Draft methods, results, or discussion sections following your conventions
No


semantic-pipeline
Compute word/sentence/document-level semantic diversity measures (DSI, SBERT, chamfer distinctness) on a parquet of texts
OPENAI_API_KEY for the document-level step; dedicated Python venv


wbl-form-filler
Fill Wharton Behavioral Lab study submission forms on JotForm
Wharton-specific; all defaults need replacing


zotero-fetch
Fetch a Zotero collection’s items and PDFs to a local folder so Claude can read them
ZOTERO_API_KEY, ZOTERO_USER_ID in your shell env

title: Skills
text:
Install flow

cp -r skills/<name> ~/.claude/skills/
grep {{ ~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md — if this returns hits, edit the file and replace placeholders.
Restart Claude Code. The skill fires as /<name>.

title: Claude Code for Researchers
text:
This site packages a working Claude Code setup for empirical research: the slide deck, a CLAUDE.md template, and 18 ready-to-install skills.
Everything is free to fork, adapt, and re-share.

title: Claude Code for Researchers
text:
Start here
If you have never used Claude Code before:

Install Claude Code. Follow the official install guide.
Install WisprFlow (optional but recommended). Talking beats typing.
Copy the CLAUDE.md template. Grab TEMPLATE_CLAUDE.md, fill in your own role, projects, and preferences, then save it to ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md. No other setup step pays off as much.
Install one skill. Pick one from the skills page that matches something you already do by hand. /pipeline-audit is a good first choice if you write papers; /data-analysis is a good first choice if you don’t.

title: Claude Code for Researchers
text:
Installing a skill
# From this repo's root:
cp -r skills/pipeline-audit ~/.claude/skills/
Restart Claude Code. The skill is now callable as /pipeline-audit.
12 of the 18 skills need configuration before first use. Grep for {{ in a SKILL.md to find placeholder variables: paths, phone numbers, credentials. The “Needs config?” column on the skills page lists the API keys, CLIs, and accounts required by each skill.

Skills — 18 installable slash commands

title: Claude Code for Researchers
text:
About the walkthrough
Intended reader: an empirical researcher who runs studies, analyzes data, and writes papers. The material assumes roughly the skill level of a third-year PhD student in psychology.
Running example: a joke-writing task with AI assistance, agency measures, and peer ratings. The walkthrough builds the task first in Qualtrics, then rebuilds it as a self-hosted web app to show why self-hosting matters for reproducibility.
Format: roughly 50 minutes of live work across four sections (setup, survey design, data analysis, writing), plus 10 minutes of questions. Nothing is pre-recorded.

title: CLAUDE.md Template
text:
A starter template for your global ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md. Copy this to ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md and fill in the bracketed placeholders.
The structure below is opinionated — it’s the one Ben uses. Adapt freely. The goal is to give Claude enough stable context about who you are, what you’re working on, and how you prefer to work that you don’t have to re-explain yourself every session.



This file defines how to work with me effectively across professional and personal contexts.
Default assumption: Professional mode unless the request clearly relates to personal life.
Primary goal: help me execute quickly, think clearly, and ship high-quality work.




Name: [Your name] Role: [Your current role — e.g., PhD student, postdoc, assistant professor, industry researcher] Fields: [Your disciplines — e.g., social psychology × decision science × marketing]
Core strengths: - [Strength 1] - [Strength 2] - [Strength 3]
Core working style: - [Preference 1 — e.g., direct, skeptical reasoning] - [Preference 2 — e.g., minimal fluff] - [Preference 3 — e.g., code-first explanations] - [Preference 4 — e.g., concrete next steps preferred]
If an assumption looks weak, challenge it.







[Top priority]
[Second priority]
[Third priority]
[Fourth priority]

Rule: if tradeoffs appear, optimize for these first.





[What does “a good week” look like? One sentence.]








Used for: [e.g., research, coding, writing, modeling, teaching]
Behavior: - [e.g., concise, analytical, high signal] - [e.g., prioritize progress over perfection] - [e.g., propose actionable next steps]



Used for: [e.g., family, fitness, routines, personal planning]
Behavior: - [e.g., practical and realistic] - [e.g., account for limited time/energy] - [e.g., avoid over-optimization]







Main question you’re trying to answer (research) or problem you’re trying to solve (industry): > [One sentence.]
Recurring themes you care about: - [Theme 1] - [Theme 2] - [Theme 3]
Primary disciplines / domains: - [Discipline 1] - [Discipline 2]




For each active project, give Claude an abstract-length description. This is the single most useful thing in your CLAUDE.md — it means Claude knows what you’re working on without you explaining.


Abstract: [2-4 sentences describing the project’s question, method, and status.] [status: current stage — e.g., “piloting Study 2”, “under review at X journal”, “drafting”]



Abstract: […] [status: …]
[Add more as needed.]





Languages: - [e.g., R (tidyverse)] - [e.g., Python] - [e.g., JS/Node as needed]
Principles: - [e.g., modular over monolithic] - [e.g., readable over clever] - [e.g., iteration speed over premature abstraction] - [e.g., cache expensive calls] - [e.g., save intermediate artifacts]
Typical stack: - [Describe the tools and glue you usually reach for]
Explanation preference: - [e.g., intuition → code → (optional) math]
[Add any strong technical opinions Claude should respect. Examples:] - [e.g., “Use lavaan for mediation, not the mediation package”] - [e.g., “Prefer parquet over CSV for large tables”] - [e.g., “Always pin dependencies”]





[Target audience — e.g., “marketing/management audiences unless specified”]
[Tone — e.g., “concise, confident prose”]
[Structural rules — e.g., “strong topic sentence for every paragraph”]
[Anti-patterns — e.g., “avoid passive voice”, “no em-dashes”, “always quantify — don’t say ‘many’ when you can say ‘63%’”]





[Describe any teaching commitments, mentees, or advising relationships Claude should know about so it can contextualize tasks that touch this work.]




Goals: - [Career target 1] - [Career target 2]
Considerations: - [e.g., job-market positioning, timing constraints]




[Add anything else that will matter across many sessions — e.g., accessibility needs, hardware constraints, regulatory context, institutional affiliations that shape what you can/can’t do.]







[Describe only if relevant to how Claude should help you — e.g., “young child at home, evenings compressed.”]



[Describe only if relevant to planning — e.g., “strength + cardio, time-efficient workouts.”]



[Only if relevant to planning or routines.]





When uncertain: - [e.g., choose simplicity] - [e.g., ship minimal viable version first]
Common reminders that help: - [“You’re optimizing before validating.”] - [“What’s the smallest version that works?”]




[Your own recurring failure modes. Being honest about these makes Claude much more useful.]
Watch for: - [e.g., overcommitting] - [e.g., perfectionism slowing execution]
Helpful intervention: - [e.g., reduce scope] - [e.g., force practical tradeoffs]




Responses should: 1. [e.g., get to the point quickly] 2. [e.g., give concrete recommendations] 3. [e.g., include tradeoffs briefly] 4. [e.g., prefer structured outputs when useful]
Avoid: - [e.g., generic motivational talk] - [e.g., excessive caveats] - [e.g., unnecessary verbosity]




If you use the plate-check and log-off skills in this repo, they expect a workspace directory with these three files:

comms.md — async channel. Claude leaves you questions in this file; you answer when you have time instead of being interrupted mid-task. Newest entry at the top.
todo.md — running task list Claude updates as you work.
current_state.md — handoff doc written at end of session so the next one picks up cold.

Point both skills at your workspace directory by replacing {WORKSPACE} in their SKILL.md files with your actual path.




[Your own running rules. Examples:]

Communicate through comms.md in the workspace folder. Put the newest entry at the top. Add date + time to every entry.
Add all my requests to todo.md so I can check whether they were completed.
Before finishing work, clean up — delete non-permanent files, clean up auxiliary artifacts.
Before handing off, render and run everything. Don’t tell me “ready to run” if you haven’t actually run it.

Always follow these instructions.
